components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main action on a screen: create task, invite member, complete setup.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #2F6F5E; color: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #2F6F5E; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; font: 650 14px/1.2 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 150ms ease-out, border-color 150ms ease-out, box-shadow 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #225346; border-color: #225346; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2F6F5E; outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(47, 111, 94, 0.18); } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #17382F; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { background: #DDE4DE; border-color: #DDE4DE; color: #6F7C76; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A supporting action that should remain visible without competing with the primary CTA.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #FFFFFF; color: #1F2523; border: 1px solid #DDE4DE; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 14px; font: 650 14px/1.2 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 150ms ease-out, border-color 150ms ease-out, box-shadow 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #F2F5F1; border-color: #C6CEC9; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2F6F5E; outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(47, 111, 94, 0.18); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { background: #E5F1EC; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: A compact status marker for ready, blocked, due soon, waiting, or done states.
components.css: .ds-chip-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; width: fit-content; min-height: 24px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 999px; background: #E5F1EC; color: #2F6F5E; font: 650 13px/1.25 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.name: Task Card
components.html:
Change HVAC filter

Due this weekend - assigned to Alex

Ready
components.css: .ds-task-card { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; background: #FFFFFF; color: #1F2523; border: 1px solid #DDE4DE; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; font-family: 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-task-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 4px 8px rgba(31, 37, 35, 0.06); } .ds-task-card h3 { margin: 0 0 4px; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.3; font-weight: 650; } .ds-task-card p { margin: 0; color: #4F5D58; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.4; } .ds-task-card span { flex: 0 0 auto; border-radius: 999px; background: #E5F1EC; color: #2F6F5E; padding: 4px 10px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 650; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: The default form field for task titles, household names, and filters.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 6px; color: #1F2523; font-family: 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field span { font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.25; font-weight: 650; } .ds-field input { background: #FFFFFF; color: #1F2523; border: 1px solid #DDE4DE; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; font: 400 16px/1.4 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2F6F5E; outline-offset: 2px; border-color: #2F6F5E; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(47, 111, 94, 0.18); }

components.name: Navigation Item
components.description: A simple app navigation item with a readable active state.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 36px; padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: 8px; color: #4F5D58; text-decoration: none; font: 650 14px/1.25 'Nunito Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 150ms ease-out, color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: #F2F5F1; color: #1F2523; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2F6F5E; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: #E5F1EC; color: #2F6F5E; }

narrative.overview: HomeOps should feel like the shared household clipboard on the kitchen counter: clear, current, plain-spoken, and easy for anyone in the home to act on. The default experience is friendly and approachable, with enough structure underneath to grow into a more information-dense console for power users later.
keyCharacteristics: Calm task surfaces with visible status, ownership, and due timing.
Density can increase through a future view setting without changing brand identity.
Premium project planning gets a distinct accent, but the free chore and maintenance core stays primary.

rules.name: The Friendly Restraint Rule
rules.body: Green is the main product color, but it should occupy less than 10 percent of a normal task screen. Its job is to identify action and state, not decorate the interface.

rules.name: The Premium Reservation Rule
rules.body: Violet is forbidden for core chores, maintenance, and errands. It only appears when a future project-planning feature is explicitly premium or outcome-based.

rules.name: The Plain Words Rule
rules.body: Use household language first: "Due soon", "Blocked by weather", "Assigned to Maya", not system-first language like "dependency state" or "workflow status".

rules.name: The No Fluid Type Rule
rules.body: Product UI type uses fixed rem or px steps. Responsive behavior changes layout and density, not the meaning of the type scale.

rules.name: The Flat Until Needed Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat. Shadows appear for interaction, focus, floating layers, or clear hierarchy. Never pair a decorative wide shadow with a 1px ghost-card border.

dos: Do make the default mode feel like The Helpful Home Clipboard: readable, human, and obvious.
Do support a future Calm Household Console mode through density, columns, and saved views, not a different visual brand.
Do use Household Green for primary actions, current selection, and meaningful ready/complete signals.
Do reserve Project Violet for future premium project planning.
Do use plain-language empty states that teach the next household action.
Do keep focus states visible and WCAG AA contrast intact.
donts: Don't make HomeOps feel like an over-optimized enterprise dashboard.
Don't make it feel like a technical admin console.
Don't make it feel like a power-user productivity tool that hides basic actions behind dense configuration.
Don't use decorative gradient text, glassmorphism, oversized hero metrics, or generic identical icon-card grids.
Don't use full-saturation accents on inactive states.
Don't use Project Violet for free core chores, maintenance, or errands.
